title: #164 initial-condition screen, variant A -- the as-committed (pre-#164) mc-output-accuracy bench, instrumented with a settled-node dump
claim: Variant A of the four-variant initial-condition screen behind issue #164: the mc-output-accuracy bench EXACTLY AS IT WAS COMMITTED BEFORE #164 (EN a DC level, `tran 10u 3m` with no `uic`, so an unconstrained ngspice operating-point solve chooses where the 3 ms transient starts), re-run on the same netlist body, the same seed (20260817) and the same N (200) as record 20260925-110312-8280915, with 14 extra hierarchical `.meas` cards added for the sole purpose of dumping the settled node set of every sample. What it is evidence FOR: that the ~6 % of draws which settle with VOUT at the input rail are not circuit states at all, and therefore not a second stable equilibrium of this loop. What it is evidence AGAINST: reading a settled transient as independent proof of an equilibrium when that transient inherited a suspect `.op` as its initial condition. SUBSTANTIATES NO SPEC ROW. This is diagnostic evidence for design/README.md's "#164" section (the four-variant initial-condition screen), deliberately kept in its own experiment slug so that measurements/build_characterization_report.py -- which reads the LEXICOGRAPHICALLY LAST record under sim/<slug>/records/ for the slug a spec row maps to -- cannot ever pick a screen variant up as the Output row's evidence. EVIDENCE_MAP maps "Output" to sim/mc-output-accuracy and nothing maps to this slug, the same way sim/pdk-smoke is harness-only rather than a spec claim. The shipped, spec-substantiating Output-row bench and record are sim/mc-output-accuracy and 20260925-131502-808cece (variant C of this same screen); nothing here supersedes, re-grades or replaces them. The vout_ss card keeps the ratified +-2% window verbatim anyway, so this variant's pass/fail tally is directly comparable with sim/mc-output-accuracy's records -- comparability is the point of the screen.

mc_corner.note: The same single mismatch-enabled point sim/mc-output-accuracy characterizes (tt_mm, 27 C, VIN 3.3 V, 1 mA) -- held fixed across all four screen variants on purpose: the screen varies the INITIAL CONDITION and nothing else.

mc_analysis.note: SCREEN VARIANT A -- the pre-#164 contract, reproduced deliberately: no `uic`, so ngspice's unconstrained `.op` seeds the transient, and EN is a DC level rather than an edge. This is the configuration under test, NOT a recommended bench. Compare with variant B (same deck plus an `.ic` seeded at regulation), variant D (same deck plus `uic`) and variant C (the shipped bench, sim/mc-output-accuracy).

mc_measurements.name: vout_ss
mc_measurements.spice: .meas tran vout_ss avg v(vout) from=2.5m to=3m
mc_measurements.note: Steady-state VOUT averaged over the settled tail (2.5ms-3ms of a 3ms transient), identical card and identical ratified window (spec/target-spec.md "Output", 1.8V +-2%, ratified by issue #1 / DR-006) to the one sim/mc-output-accuracy uses -- kept identical so this screen variant's tally is comparable with that bench's records. This slug substantiates no spec row; see the experiment claim.

mc_measurements.name: fb_ss
mc_measurements.spice: .meas tran fb_ss avg v(xldo.fb) from=2.5m to=3m
mc_measurements.note: Node dump (unbounded -- diagnostic, no limit and therefore no verdict): settled V(xldo.fb), averaged over the same tail as vout_ss. Why this node: the divider tap the error amp compares against VREF -- the node whose 668-1984 V (and 1.3e15 V) settled values are the whole finding: FB is fed ONLY by VOUT through a passive three-leg res_xhigh_po string, so any realizable state has 0 <= V(N_FBB) <= V(FB) <= V(VOUT) <= VIN.

mc_measurements.note: Node dump (unbounded -- diagnostic, no limit and therefore no verdict): settled V(xldo.n_fbb), averaged over the same tail as vout_ss. Why this node: the divider's lower tap -- second half of the same algebra check.

Why this node: the error amp's output, i.e. the pass device's gate: #164 Scope item 1 asked what holds it low enough to keep the pass device fully on.

Why this node: the Miller/compensation node (R_CZ's far end) -- one of the three res_xhigh_po instances ngspice names in its singular-matrix warnings.
